description: Canonical threat actors for EdgeGuard: one entry per actor with its canonical key (the ThreatActor name EdgeGuard writes, normalised like node_identity.canonicalize_merge_key), its ATT&CK group id and the synonyms that name it. Built by scripts/build_canonical_threat_actors.py from the MISP galaxy threat-actor clusters and the ATT&CK version EdgeGuard loaded, with the hand-reviewed decisions of canonical_threat_actor_overrides.json applied last. Names listed under 'ambiguous' point to more than one actor, or were marked never_merge, and are never merged.

inputs.used: the names of the ATT&CK-sourced ThreatActor nodes, and the aliases and group ids of the records MITRE delivered for them (the ATT&CK version EdgeGuard loaded)

attribution.source: MISP galaxy (threat-actor, mitre-intrusion-set, microsoft-activity-group, 360net-threat-actor and mitre-ics-groups galaxies)
MITRE ATT&CK (group names, ids, aliases and revocations, from the mitre-intrusion-set galaxy and from the ATT&CK version EdgeGuard loaded)

rules: Records with the same ATT&CK id are one actor named after the ATT&CK group; a record whose own name is the ATT&CK name of a different group is not anchored by its id. A group ATT&CK revoked into another is folded into its successor (origin mitre_revoked). The ATT&CK version EdgeGuard loaded anchors too: its names and the aliases MITRE delivered for them are the strongest claims after an actor key (origin mitre_loaded), and a group the galaxy copy does not have is anchored by its name.

A record without an ATT&CK id joins an anchored actor only when its name (for the 360net-threat-actor galaxy also the name without its ' - APT-C-NN' id) is that actor's key, an ATT&CK alias or revoked name of it or the name of a record anchored to it, for exactly one actor; names that differ only in spaces, hyphens, dots or underscores are the same name. Otherwise records with the same name form an actor of their own; a 360net-threat-actor record that joins no ATT&CK actor is left out.

A name claimed by several actors goes to the actor whose own name it is (actor key, then loaded ATT&CK alias, then galaxy ATT&CK alias, revoked name or record name, then galaxy synonym); a tie makes it ambiguous. Spellings of one name held by different actors stay with the actor holding the strongest spelling and are ambiguous for the others (all of them on a tie). ATT&CK ids, placeholder names and lists of names are not synonyms; a synonym is taken as EdgeGuard's actor-name hygiene writes it.

Suffix rule: the variant with or without a trailing ' group' / ' team' of an actor key or ATT&CK name is a synonym when no other actor claims it, and ambiguous when another actor holds it only by a galaxy synonym (a shortened name keeps at least three characters and a letter; nothing is added to a name that already contains 'group' or 'team').
Overrides are applied last: never_merge with an actor, merge, never_merge, canonical_name.

never_merge.reason: Common words that only the suffix rule derives, from 'Comment Group' (APT1), 'Tsar Team' (APT28), 'Beijing Group' (Elderwood), 'Iron Group' and 'Hacking Team'. As bare names they do not identify one actor.

Doubtful: the node's only malware link is 'green lambert - s0690', an unrelated ATT&CK malware family that looks like a bad extraction (the name appears inside 'Lambert'); merging would carry that link to the gang. Its report and that of 'bert ransomware' describe the same gang, so revisit once the extraction is fixed.

A malware family name. ATT&CK lists 'BlackEnergy (Group)' as an alias of Sandworm Team (G0034); EdgeGuard's actor-name hygiene drops the parenthetical, which leaves the malware's name, so the bare name is not taken as the group ('blackenergy group' still is).
